answer: Peer-prediction scoring makes identity itself costly. Each grader stakes a deposit; pay follows agreement with a randomly sampled panel of independent agents, not your own circle. Clones that flatter each other are almost never sampled together, so a sybil farm earns nothing while burning its stakes. Whether a grader is jade, knoll, orchard, or a fresh fake, the panel pays only when verdicts track true quality, so lazy grading loses stake each round. An attacker pays a bond per identity plus months of uncompensated history.
